title: Persistence of a finite relative mapping cone in a filtered colimit
statement:
Use the universes, coherent quasicategories, mapping spaces and homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], small filtered infinity categories and finite simplicial sets of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and left cones $K^{\triangleleft}=\Delta^0\star K$ of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $B$ be a small infinity category and $D:I\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty/B}$ a small filtered coherent diagram with structural functors $p_j:E_j\to B$. Let $p:E\to B$ with legs $r_j$ be a slice colimiting cocone whose underlying total cocone is colimiting. Fix $i\in I$, a finite simplicial set $K$, a coherent cone $q:K^{\triangleleft}\to E_i$ and its base cone $\beta=p_iq$. Write $c=q(*)$, $d=q|_K$, and $\beta_k:\beta(*)\to\beta(k)$ for its legs, including their higher cone compatibilities. For $u:i\to j$, write $c_u=D(u)c$, $d_u=D(u)d$, and $q_u=D(u)q$; the coherent structural maps to $B$ identify their base cones with $\beta$. Here, for objects $x,y$ of $E_j$ and an arrow $g:p_j(x)\to p_j(y)$ of $B$ (read through these structural identifications), $\operatorname{Map}^{g}_{E_j}(x,y)$ means the homotopy fiber over $g$ of the map $\operatorname{Map}_{E_j}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(p_j(x),p_j(y))$ induced by $p_j$; likewise $\operatorname{Map}^{g}_{E}$ is formed with $p$. Suppose that for every such $u$, every $z\in E_j$ and every base arrow $h:p_j(z)\to\beta(*)$, postcomposition with the legs of $q_u$ gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E_j}^{h}(z,c_u)\longrightarrow\lim_{k\in K}\operatorname{Map}_{E_j}^{\beta_k h}(z,d_u(k)).$$
The diagram of spaces on the right uses postcomposition along $d_u$ and the compatibilities in $\beta$. Then for every $z\in E$ and $h:p(z)\to\beta(*)$, the image cone $r_iq$ gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E}^{h}(z,r_ic)\longrightarrow\lim_{k\in K}\operatorname{Map}_{E}^{\beta_k h}(z,r_id(k)).$$
All base-arrow identifications retain the structural coherences of the slice diagram. Empty $K$ is allowed; its limit is a terminal space. No operad, cocartesian-lift existence, or full faithfulness of transition functors is assumed.

No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Fix $z\in E$ and $h:p(z)\to\beta(*)$. The common-stage clause gives $b\in I$, $z_b\in E_b$ and an equivalence $r_bz_b\simeq z$. Filteredness applied to the discrete pair $i,b$ gives $a\in I$ and arrows $u:i\to a$, $w:b\to a$. Put $z_a=D(w)z_b$, $c_a=D(u)c$, and $q_a=D(u)q$. The cocone gives $r_az_a\simeq z$ and $r_aq_a\simeq r_iq$. Apply $p$ and the structural equivalences to obtain $p_a(z_a)\simeq p(z)$ and $p_a(c_a)\simeq\beta(*)$. Composing $h$ with these equivalences defines $h_a:p_a(z_a)\to p_a(c_a)$. This is an arrow in the fixed base $B$, so there is no assertion that $h$ lifts to an edge of $E_a$. For $v:a\to j$, write $z_v=D(v)z_a$ and $q_v=D(v)q_a$; use the structural triangles to interpret the base arrows throughout as $h_a$ and $\beta_kh_a$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1, final mapping-space comparison, with a finite simplicial incidence shape in place of the finite discrete product; finite-space-limit argument of Proposition 3.3.2; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Let $J=I_{a/}$. The filtered mapping-space calculus says $J$ is small and filtered. Define $A_v=\operatorname{Map}_{E_j}^{h_a}(z_v,c_{vu})$ and $T(k,v)=\operatorname{Map}_{E_j}^{\beta_kh_a}(z_v,d_{vu}(k))$, where the superscripts use the structural identifications from step 1. Its natural homotopy-fiber comparisons give $\operatorname{colim}_J A_v\simeq\operatorname{Map}_E^h(z,r_ic)$ and $\operatorname{colim}_J T(k,v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_E^{\beta_kh}(z,r_id(k))$. The postcomposition naturality, including all higher compatibilities, makes the latter comparisons a comparison of $K$-diagrams. In particular it identifies the maps from the $A_v$ induced by the cone legs, rather than merely identifying their source and target spaces separately.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1, final mapping-space comparison, with a finite simplicial incidence shape in place of the finite discrete product; finite-space-limit argument of Proposition 3.3.2; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For each $v:a\to j$, the composite $vu:i\to j$ is one of the arrows quantified in the hypothesis. Apply that hypothesis with $z_v$ and the base arrow obtained from $h_a$ by the structural identifications. It gives precisely the equivalence $A_v\to\lim_{k\in K}T(k,v)$ induced by $q_{vu}$. These maps form a coherent transformation in $v$: a triangle in $J$ acts by the given functor $D$ on $z_v$ and $q_{vu}$, so its map on mapping spaces commutes with each postcomposition leg; its higher simplices give the same compatibility for higher triangles. Thus the transformation is pointwise an equivalence, and its colimit is an equivalence (apply the colimit functor to its inverse equivalence in the functor category).

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1, final mapping-space comparison, with a finite simplicial incidence shape in place of the finite discrete product; finite-space-limit argument of Proposition 3.3.2; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Apply the spaces comparison with $\kappa=\aleph_0$, the small filtered $J$, the finite simplicial set $K$, and $T:K\times J\to\mathcal S$. It identifies $\operatorname{colim}_J\lim_KT$ with $\lim_K\operatorname{colim}_JT$. Composing it with step 3 and the comparisons of step 2 gives $\operatorname{Map}_E^h(z,r_ic)\simeq\lim_{k\in K}\operatorname{Map}_E^{\beta_kh}(z,r_id(k))$. Each comparison is induced by the cocone and postcomposition by its actual legs, so the composite is the map of the image cone in the statement, with its structural base coherences. For $K=\varnothing$, the same spaces theorem identifies the filtered colimit of terminal spaces with a terminal space; step 1 still applies to $z,c$. No nonempty-shape hypothesis was used. Since $z,h$ were arbitrary this proves the assertion.
